title.rendered: Forget Not All His Benefits: Remembering Everything He Has Done | The Thankful Heart, Day 10

excerpt.rendered: Psalm 103:1-5 tells our soul to bless the Lord and forget not all His benefits. Day 10 of The Thankful Heart remembers everything He has done.

content.rendered:
David did not wait for his feelings to lead him into worship. He spoke to his own soul and told it what to do: bless the Lord, and do not forget. Sometimes thanksgiving begins with a sermon we preach to ourselves.

The Gospel For Today | Tuesday, November 24, 2026 | The Thankful Heart, Day 10

Today’s Scripture

“Bless the Lord, O my soul; and all that is within me, bless His holy name! Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all His benefits: who forgives all your iniquities, who heals all your diseases, who redeems your life from destruction, who crowns you with lovingkindness and tender mercies, who satisfies your mouth with good things, so that your youth is renewed like the eagle’s.”
Psalm 103:1-5 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Psalm 103 opens with David talking to himself. “Bless the Lord, O my soul.” He says it twice. Perhaps his soul was slow to respond. Perhaps, like us, he found that worries crowd out worship if they are left unchecked. So he took hold of his own heart and pointed it toward God.

Then comes the key phrase: “and forget not all His benefits.” The word translated “benefits” is the Hebrew gemul (גְּמוּל). In English, benefits can sound like perks on a list, but gemul means a dealing, what one person has actually done toward another: here, everything God has done for us. Elsewhere the same word often means a repayment of what was deserved, which makes verse 10 all the more striking: He has not dealt with us according to our sins. Forgetfulness is one of the great enemies of gratitude. We remember the one thing that went wrong and forget the hundred things God did right. The bill we cannot pay looms larger than the years He has provided. David’s cure is simple. Make a list. Name the benefits one by one.

And what a list it is. He forgives all your iniquities. Not some. All. He heals all your diseases. He redeems your life from destruction. He crowns you with lovingkindness and tender mercies. He satisfies your mouth with good things. Read through it and notice that every one of these benefits finds its fullness in Jesus. At the cross He bore our sins (1 Peter 2:24). By His stripes we were healed. He redeemed us, not with silver or gold, but with His own precious blood (1 Peter 1:18-19). The benefits David sang about, we now hold in Christ.

Notice too the picture of being crowned. The God who lifted you out of destruction does not leave you in the gutter, cleaned up but still on the ground. He places a crown on your head: lovingkindness and tender mercies. You are not a beggar who has been tolerated. You are a child who has been honoured. That is worth remembering.

So today, do what David did. Speak to your soul, wherever you are, on a bus in London or at a desk in Dubai. Say, “Bless the Lord, O my soul.” Then name His benefits. Forgiven. Healed. Redeemed. Crowned. Satisfied. Renewed. Count them out on your fingers if you need to. A remembering heart is a thankful heart.

How the Thankful Heart Remembers

It speaks to its own soul. David told his heart to bless the Lord before he felt like it.

It refuses to forget. Gratitude names the benefits one by one.

It sees the benefits in Christ. Forgiveness, healing and redemption are ours through His finished work.

Declaration

Bless the Lord, O my soul, and all that is within me, bless His holy name. Lord, I will not forget Your benefits. I thank You that You have forgiven all my iniquities and healed all my diseases (Psalm 103:3), and that by the stripes of Jesus I was healed (1 Peter 2:24). I thank You that You have redeemed my life from destruction, crowned me with lovingkindness and tender mercies, and satisfied my mouth with good things. My youth is renewed like the eagle’s. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
